sections.strategy: M&S made its first-ever London Fashion Week appearance on 19 September, marking 100 years of M&S fashion with a runway show spanning Collection, Per Una and Autograph; all 59 looks shown were available to buy immediately online across the UK and Europe and in 10 flagship stores. Store transformation continued with the reopened Chiswick shop (75% larger at 15,200 sq ft, adding a bakery, flower shop, sushi counter and barista coffee) and a £7m tripling of the Wheatley store, both part of the wider format-upgrade programme alongside newer Foodhall-led openings.
sections.pricing: Shares traded around 371p (24 September), with the average 12-month analyst price target at 432.50p and a 'Moderate Buy' consensus (6 buy, 2 hold across 8 brokerages). Berenberg reissued a Buy rating with a 480p target citing the Fashion Week appearance, while Goldman Sachs trimmed its target to 470p from 490p; Peel Hunt separately flagged that food sales are 'flying' but fashion remains 'hungover' from last year's cyberattack.
sections.launches: The London Fashion Week collection functioned as this week's headline launch — a 'see now, buy now' capsule across Collection, Per Una and Autograph timed to the fashion-week slot rather than a standard seasonal drop.
sections.gossip: City commentary this week centred on the widening gap between M&S's food performance (strong, gaining share) and fashion (still working through the cyberattack's 'long tail'), with analysts split between rewarding the Fashion Week publicity push (Berenberg) and trimming targets on execution risk (Goldman Sachs).
soWhat: The 'see now, buy now' Fashion Week format — 59 looks live for purchase same-day — signals M&S wants suppliers who can compress runway-to-shelf lead times further; speed-to-market capability is becoming a differentiator for vendor selection.

Analysts still describe fashion as 'hungover' from the cyberattack even as food outperforms — near-term clothing order volumes may stay cautious until the division demonstrates a clean quarter, a signal worth watching for order-book pacing.

No supplier-map, Plan A, or sourcing-mix news surfaced this week — the India/Sri Lanka/Bangladesh/Turkey/China balance and OSH disclosure remain unchanged, consistent with M&S's twice-yearly review cadence rather than continuous updates.

Continued capital going into store format (Chiswick, Wheatley) is food-and-format-led rather than fashion-specific, suggesting near-term M&S investment priority remains grocery footprint over incremental clothing floor space.
